response.reason: The closed FCSTM shows PumpControl.PumpRegion, WaterRegion, MethaneRegion (and their PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState leaves) are all unreachable from root; only PumpControl and a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state are reachable, and UnspecifiedInitial is a dead-end leaf. This produces distinct owner-entry, root-reachability, and dead-end defects layered on top of the NL1 initial-entry contract (which is otherwise satisfied) and the NL3/NL4/NL5 action/endpoint contracts (which cannot be reached, but existence of endpoints is a separate property from reachability). I derive one owner-level initial_entry contract (PumpControl -> PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState default entry is fine locally, but PumpControl's own default entry goes to UnspecifiedInitial, a synthetic dead-end, not to any of the three declared operating substates), and separate reachability candidates for each of the three operating regions/states, since none is reachable from root despite being declared as the system's core NL3/NL4/NL5 behavior. I keep NL1's satisfied root->PumpControl edge separate from this defect (that edge is exact and correct). I also flag the PumpControl default local entry going to UnspecifiedInitial (a synthetic leaf, not any of PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState) as a new derived initial_entry defect at the PumpControl owner scope, since PumpControl's own [*] edge (line 16 in FCSTM) targets a synthetic dead-end rather than entering one of the three semantically required substates/regions, causing the entire declared operating behavior of NL3/NL4/NL5 to be permanently unreachable. This is a genuine causal property not visible from the NL-only contract extraction (it requires the closed FCSTM reachability graph), hence one additional_contracts row. I do not add a deadlock_freedom candidate for the individual PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState leaves since NL3/4/5 state_action contracts do not establish explicit progress/continuation obligations beyond the action itself, and V1 requires an explicit progress obligation which is absent; but I do add a V1 candidate for the reachable UnspecifiedInitial dead-end because that leaf is reachable and has zero outgoing transitions, directly matching the LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING deterministic fact under the derived owner-entry contract's semantic scope.

arguments.reason: The closed FCSTM shows PumpControl.PumpRegion, WaterRegion, MethaneRegion (and their PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState leaves) are all unreachable from root; only PumpControl and a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state are reachable, and UnspecifiedInitial is a dead-end leaf. This produces distinct owner-entry, root-reachability, and dead-end defects layered on top of the NL1 initial-entry contract (which is otherwise satisfied) and the NL3/NL4/NL5 action/endpoint contracts (which cannot be reached, but existence of endpoints is a separate property from reachability). I derive one owner-level initial_entry contract (PumpControl -> PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState default entry is fine locally, but PumpControl's own default entry goes to UnspecifiedInitial, a synthetic dead-end, not to any of the three declared operating substates), and separate reachability candidates for each of the three operating regions/states, since none is reachable from root despite being declared as the system's core NL3/NL4/NL5 behavior. I keep NL1's satisfied root->PumpControl edge separate from this defect (that edge is exact and correct). I also flag the PumpControl default local entry going to UnspecifiedInitial (a synthetic leaf, not any of PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState) as a new derived initial_entry defect at the PumpControl owner scope, since PumpControl's own [*] edge (line 16 in FCSTM) targets a synthetic dead-end rather than entering one of the three semantically required substates/regions, causing the entire declared operating behavior of NL3/NL4/NL5 to be permanently unreachable. This is a genuine causal property not visible from the NL-only contract extraction (it requires the closed FCSTM reachability graph), hence one additional_contracts row. I do not add a deadlock_freedom candidate for the individual PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState leaves since NL3/4/5 state_action contracts do not establish explicit progress/continuation obligations beyond the action itself, and V1 requires an explicit progress obligation which is absent; but I do add a V1 candidate for the reachable UnspecifiedInitial dead-end because that leaf is reachable and has zero outgoing transitions, directly matching the LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING deterministic fact under the derived owner-entry contract's semantic scope.

stage_receipts.reason: Five numbered segments establish: (1) root initial entry into PumpControl (context-setting sentence about transitioning to different substates based on conditions, no exact endpoints yet), (2) containment of three substates within PumpControl, (3) initial entry into PumpState within PumpControl plus its activation action, (4) transition group alternative from PumpState to WaterState plus its monitoring action, (5) transition group alternative from WaterState(or PumpState) to MethaneState plus its monitoring action. Discourse resolution: NL1 introduces PumpControl as root state entered initially; NL3 "system first transitions to PumpState" is owner-local initial entry into PumpControl's substate PumpState, not a root-to-substate transition since NL2 already established PumpControl containing the three substates. NL4 "can also transition to WaterState" continues from PumpState per sequential discourse convention (first enter A; also transition to B). NL5 "similarly...transition to MethaneState" continues from WaterState. These three form one shared-source group family: PumpState as source with alternatives WaterState and MethaneState (both reachable from PumpState per the sequential "also"/"similarly" pattern establishing PumpState as continuing source). No explicit guards/events distinguish alternatives; "based on specific conditions" in NL1 is broad capability context, not an exact guard. No disjointness contract emitted since no explicit distinguishability requirement stated beyond generic "based on specific conditions" which is too vague to bind. Termination not established. No cardinality contract since three substates are named explicitly (explicit_named_members) - but no numeric requirement stated distinctly from containment, so no separate cardinality contract needed beyond containment (the count of three is implicit in naming, not a separately stated required-count obligation distinct from the containment itself); however per schema, cardinality property must be independently required - here NL2 states "three main substates" which is an explicit count requirement, so a cardinality contract is warranted with explicit_named_members domain.
